words.meaning: The curved path of a celestial object or spacecraft round a star, planet, or moon.
words.sentence1: The satellite successfully entered a stable orbit around the Earth. (The satellite successfully entered a stable orbit around the Earth.)
words.sentence2: Scientists calculated the exact orbit of the distant comet. (Scientists calculated the exact orbit of the distant comet.)

words.meaning: An obscuring of the light from one celestial body by the passage of another between it and the observer or between it and its source.
words.sentence1: El eclipse solar fascinó a millones de personas en todo el mundo. (The solar eclipse fascinated millions of people around the world.)
words.sentence2: Esperamos ansiosos el próximo eclipse lunar para usar nuestros telescopios. (We eagerly await the next lunar eclipse to use our telescopes.)

words.meaning: A cloud of gas and dust in outer space, visible in the night sky either as an indistinct bright patch or as a dark silhouette.
words.sentence1: Cette belle nebuleuse est situee a des annees-lumiere de notre systeme solaire. (This beautiful nebula is located light-years away from our solar system.)
words.sentence2: L'astronome a capture l'image d'une jeune nebuleuse avec son puissant telescope. (The astronomer captured the image of a young nebula with his powerful telescope.)

words.meaning: A system of millions or billions of stars, together with gas and dust, held together by gravitational attraction.
words.sentence1: Unsere Milchstrasse ist nur eine von Milliarden Galaxien im Universum. (Our Milky Way is just one of billions of galaxies in the universe.)
words.sentence2: Mit dem neuen Weltraumteleskop konnten Astronomen eine sehr alte Galaxie entdecken. (With the new space telescope, astronomers were able to discover a very old galaxy.)

words.meaning: A shooting star or meteor passing through the atmosphere.
words.sentence1: Yozora o miageta toki, kireina ryusei ga nagareta. (When I looked up at the night sky, a beautiful shooting star streaked across.)
words.sentence2: Kondo no yoru wa ryusei-gun o kansoku suru yotei desu. (We plan to observe the meteor shower on the upcoming night.)

words.meaning: A group of stars forming a recognizable pattern that is traditionally named after its apparent form or identified with a mythological figure.
words.sentence1: Orione e una delle costellazioni piu facili da riconoscere nel cielo notturno. (Orion is one of the easiest constellations to recognize in the night sky.)
words.sentence2: Gli antichi marinai usavano la costellazione dell'Orsa Maggiore per orientarsi in mare. (Ancient sailors used the constellation of the Great Bear to navigate at sea.)

words.meaning: Stars in the night sky, heavenly bodies.
words.sentence1: Wǎnshàng de xīngchén zài yèkōng zhōng shǎnyào. (The stars are sparkling in the night sky.)
words.sentence2: Tā yǎngwàng zhè piàn chōngmǎn xīngchén de yǔzhòu. (He looks up at this universe full of stars.)

words.meaning: A shooting star or meteor burning brightly in the night sky.
words.sentence1: Bame haneuleseo binnaneun yuseongeul bomyeo sowoneul bielda. (I made a wish while watching a shooting star shining in the night sky.)
words.sentence2: Ibeon jumareun yuseongugeul gwancheokhagi joheun nalsida. (This weekend is great weather for observing a meteor shower.)

words.meaning: Star or heavenly body in the expanse of the cosmos.
words.sentence1: Tarakar chorsal chenh cheun kampong cherng phnom yub nih. (The stars are shining brightly at the foot of the mountain tonight.)
words.sentence2: Kneat khernh tarakar mouy tol thleakh chus mk kraom. (He saw a star falling down towards the ground.)

words.meaning: A celestial body moving about the sun, consisting of a central nucleus surrounded by a nebulous envelope and usually having a tail.
words.sentence1: Die helder komeet was vir 'n paar weke lank met die blote oog sigbaar. (The bright comet was visible to the naked eye for a few weeks.)
words.sentence2: Wetenskaplikes bestudeer die samestelling van die komeet se stert. (Scientists are studying the composition of the comet's tail.)
